paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Jesus gives the Twelve power and authority, and then He sends them out with almost nothing in their hands. He tells them, "Take nothing for the journey…" (Luke 9:3). The power was never in the packing list, baker. It came from the One who sent them.

That matters for you, because most of us feel like we need more before we can do anything for God. More time, more knowledge, more confidence, more of EVERYTHING. I once thought a worn-out stamper in a junk drawer had nothing left to offer, and I was wrong about that! When Jesus sends, He supplies what the job needs (Luke 9:1-2).

Then there's Herod, who hears all that's happening and is perplexed. He says, "I beheaded John," and then he asks, "but who is this man I hear such things about?" (Luke 9:9). It's the biggest question in the whole passage, baker. Everybody has an answer going around, but you get to go to the Word and find out for yourself who Jesus is.
